paper_title: MAXING OUT: STOCKS AS LOTTERIES AND THE CROSS-SECTION OF EXPECTED
summary: Deprioritize. The paper (Bali, Cakici and Whitelaw) argues that stocks with extreme positive daily returns are overpriced lottery-like assets, so the lowest MAX decile should beat the highest. We tested a long-only, equal-weight version of the lowest MAX decile on a 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe over 2015 to 2025, and it returned a net CAGR of 6.31% against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe, with a Sharpe ratio of 0.35 against 0.65. The edge fails at 10 bps, holds in 0 of 2 sub-periods, and the ranked groups run the wrong way (rho 0.84), so the paper's pattern did not appear in this sample. In the fund simulation, P(NPV > 0) is 2% and the median incremental fee PV is -$5.0M against the equal-weight universe fund. The paper was read reliably, but the negative performance, weak robustness and negative economics together drive the recommendation.
